y1: “Don't think that I came to destroy the Law or the Prophets. I didn't come to destroy, but to fulfill.”
y2: At that time, the most zealous people were the Pharisees and the teachers of the law. Jesus said that to enter the kingdom of heaven, you need a righteousness that surpasses theirs. Not more rules, but a deeper heart.
y3: A 'jot' is the smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet, yodh, and a 'tittle' is a tiny stroke that distinguishes letters. Jesus didn't take the Old Testament lightly. Instead, He fulfilled the purpose the Old Testament pointed to in Himself.
y5: To the command “Do not murder,” Jesus adds: “Everyone who is angry with his brother will be subject to judgment.” Murder starts with anger in the heart and degrading words.
y6: He says to leave your gift in front of the altar and go reconcile with your brother first. Our relationship with God cannot be separated from our relationship with people.
y7: In 5:21–48, “You have heard that it was said to the people long ago... But I tell you” is repeated six times. Jesus doesn't say “so-and-so said this” like the rabbis; He says “I tell you.” This is the authority of the One who gave the Law (7:29).
y8: If forced to go one mile
y9: “Eye for eye” was actually a law that limited revenge. Jesus goes a step further: “Whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn the other to him as well.”
y10: A Roman soldier could force a person from the occupied nation to carry a load for one mile. Jesus says to go with him two miles. Turning forced labor into voluntary goodness.
y11: This doesn't mean to just endure abuse. It is an active love that breaks the chain of revenge and surprises the other person. In a dangerous situation, asking for help is also wisdom.
y13: The saying “Love your neighbor and hate your enemy” is not in the Old Testament. People had added it. Jesus says: “Love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you.”
y14: God makes His sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and on the unrighteous. Therefore He says: “You therefore shall be perfect.”
y15: “Teleios” doesn't mean flawless perfection; it means “having reached the goal, mature.” When our love expands to include our enemies, we grow as children who resemble our Father in heaven.
verse: “But I tell you, love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you, that you may be children of your Father in heaven.”
prayer: Our Father in heaven, thank You for Your love that makes the sun rise on both the evil and the good. Help me to live rightly not just on the outside, but from the heart. Give me the courage to reconcile first, and teach me to pray for the person I hate. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ, who prayed for His enemies. Amen.
d0: Law. The word 'Torah' means 'teaching, guidance.' It is not a rulebook, but the way of life for God's people. “The Law and the Prophets” is an expression referring to the entire Old Testament.
d1: righteousness. It's not a score for keeping rules, but a whole life lived rightly before God and neighbor. It is one of the key words in the Sermon on the Mount (5:6, 10, 20; 6:1, 33).
d2: altar. It was the place in the Jerusalem temple where sacrifices were offered to God. It was a three-day walk from Galilee to Jerusalem. Yet Jesus said to reconcile first.
d3: enemy. It was a word that included not only personal enemies, but also national enemies, like Roman soldiers. On the cross, Jesus prayed for those who nailed Him (Luke 23:34).
d4: perfect. It is not a flawless perfection, but a state where love has fully grown to resemble God. Luke translates the same teaching as “be merciful” (Luke 6:36).
